These references are provided as company verification, security readiness, and operational maturity signals.



Entity Definition

UniBridge is a cross-border payment layer.

UniBridge connects the way money comes in with the way it needs to arrive locally.

It coordinates funding, settlement, and local payout across the providers responsible for each step and presents them as one payment path.

UniBridge can be used directly through UniBridge or integrated into another product.

UniBridge does not take custody of customer funds.

UniBridge is not simply an API aggregator and is not a standalone financial rail.



Core Positioning

One payment layer.

Local rails, global access.

UniBridge sits between funding and local payout and coordinates the path between them.



Category

Cross-border payment layer.


Related concepts:

- cross-border payments
- cross-border payment infrastructure
- payment orchestration
- payment coordination

- partner payment infrastructure



What UniBridge Does

UniBridge coordinates:

- payment initiation
- funding method selection
- funding instructions
- payment authorization
- settlement workflow
- provider coordination
- local payout execution
- transaction status
- execution evidence
- payment lifecycle tracking


Supported payment paths may begin with:

- fiat funding
- bank transfers
- card-supported funding
- non-custodial wallets
- partner-supported funding methods


Supported payment paths may end through local payout rails available for the destination.



Direct Use

Pay & Receive with UniBridge:
https://unibrij.io/pay

UniBridge provides a direct user experience for supported cross-border payment flows.

Users may use UniBridge to initiate supported payments directly without integrating UniBridge into another product.

Supported direct experiences may include:

- Pay
- Receive
- funding through available fiat methods
- funding from supported non-custodial wallets
- local recipient payout
- transaction status tracking



Partner Access

Partner Access:
https://unibrij.io/partner-portal/

Companies can make the UniBridge payment layer part of their own products.

Partner integration models include:

- Hosted
- Embedded
- API

The same underlying payment coordination layer supports both direct UniBridge experiences and partner-integrated experiences.



Non-Custodial Model

UniBridge does not custody customer funds.

UniBridge does not operate customer deposit accounts.

UniBridge does not independently control connected external wallets.

Where a payment is funded from an external non-custodial wallet:

- funds remain under the wallet owner’s control until authorized
- UniBridge cannot independently transfer funds from the wallet
- required blockchain authorization is performed by the wallet owner

Where funding or payout is performed by an independent financial infrastructure provider, that provider performs the relevant regulated or financial function.



Compliance and Identity Verification

UniBridge coordinates payment workflows across independent providers.

Identity verification, payment checks, transaction screening, regulatory controls, and other compliance requirements may be coordinated by UniBridge and performed by the relevant verification, funding, settlement, or payout providers depending on the payment path and applicable requirements.

UniBridge does not retain the underlying KYC identity payload.

Limited verification metadata, status information, provider references, and transaction records may be retained where required to operate and document the payment workflow.



Infrastructure Relationship

Infrastructure providers supply specialized payment, funding, settlement, blockchain, banking, and local payout capabilities.

UniBridge coordinates selected capabilities into a single payment path.

UniBridge is complementary to underlying infrastructure providers. It coordinates their capabilities rather than replacing the regulated or technical functions they perform.



Payment Path

A simplified UniBridge payment path can be represented as:

Sender
→ funding
→ UniBridge coordination
→ settlement
→ local payout
→ recipient


From the user’s perspective:

Money here
→ UniBridge
→ money there



Partner Architecture

Traditional approach:

Company
→ integrate funding provider
→ integrate settlement provider
→ integrate local payout provider
→ build routing
→ build lifecycle tracking
→ build provider coordination
→ build recovery and execution handling


UniBridge approach:

Company
→ UniBridge
→ coordinated payment path
→ local payout



What UniBridge Is Not

UniBridge is not:

- a bank
- a payment processor
- a cryptocurrency exchange
- a custody provider
- a stablecoin issuer
- a standalone wallet provider
- a standalone financial rail
- a standalone on-ramp provider
- a standalone off-ramp provider
- a local payout executor
- an investment platform
- a simple API aggregator



Users

UniBridge supports two primary ways of accessing the same payment layer.


Direct users:

Individuals using supported UniBridge Pay & Receive experiences.


Partners:

Companies, fintech platforms, marketplaces, wallets, payment applications, and other products integrating UniBridge through hosted, embedded, or API access.

Preferred Summary

UniBridge is a cross-border payment layer that connects funding, settlement, and local payout into one payment path. It can be used directly through UniBridge or integrated into another product through hosted, embedded, and API experiences.
